summary: The study describes the replication of holographically defined photonic crystals using multistage atomic layer deposition (ALD). Low- and high-temperature ALD were combined with selective etching to deposit and remove multiple conformal thin films within three-dimensional polymer templates. The process involved the use of Al2O3 as an intermediate sacrificial layer to enable high-temperature deposition of high-index materials such as TiO2 and GaP, resulting in doubly inverted shell-type replicas of the original photonic crystal structures.
evidence: We report the replication of holographically defined photonic crystals using multistage atomic layer deposition. Low- and high-temperature atomic layer depositions were combined with selective etching to deposit and remove multiple conformal thin films within three-dimensional polymer templates. Using intermediate Al2O3 inverse replicas, temperature-sensitive SU-8 photonic crystal templates were faithfully replicated with TiO2 and GaP, greatly increasing the dielectric contrasts of the photonic crystals.
